newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to expand daily capacity at Norne oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to expand daily capacity at Norne oilfield.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it would expand capacity on the Norne production ship in the Norwegian Sea to 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 170,000 bpd.

The decision for the expansion was taken by the Norne licensees after a bottleneck study earlier in the year. The increase will give Norne a higher output than any other production ship currently under construction or in operation, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Shareholders in Norne are Statoil, with the government's direct financial interest, Norsk Hydro ASA, Saga Petroleum ASA, Enterprise Oil and Norsk Agip.
As a result of the expansion the number of production and injection wells at the field will be increased to 17 from 14 at a cost of about 360 million crowns.
Spare capacity will be available on Norne from late 1999 or early 2000 as a result of the expansion.
Statoil said it would drill a new exploration well on one or more identified prospects on the licence to exploit the extra capacity and to extend plateau production.
"We're hoping this well will identify additional resources that can be produced through a subsea solution tied back to Norne as early as 2000," said Kjell Helle, Statoil's operations vice president.
